urban-change-challenges-cycle.alt: A row of five boxes joined by arrows. One: lenders refuse loans or set worse terms in the neighborhood. Two: owners cannot repair or sell, so buildings decline and some are abandoned. Three: the city clears blocks for new projects, or investors buy cheap buildings. Four: new money arrives, rents and prices rise, and new shops open. Five: some long-time residents gain while others are priced out and move away. Below, policy responses: fair lending laws, inclusionary zoning, rent help and land trusts.
